questions.question_text: A car travels 100 m in 10 s at constant speed. What is its speed?
questions.markscheme_answer: Speed = distance / time = 100 m / 10 s = 10 m/s

questions.question_text: A ball is dropped from rest and falls for 3 s. How far does it fall? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.markscheme_answer: s = ½gt² = ½ × 10 × 9 = 45 m

questions.question_text:
The diagram shows the velocity–time graph of a car.


What is the average velocity of the car?
A projectile is launched at 30° above horizontal with initial speed 20 m/s. Find the maximum height reached. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.markscheme_answer: v_y = 20 sin(30°) = 10 m/s. At max height, v = 0: h = v²/(2g) = 100/20 = 5 m

questions.question_text: Two balls are thrown simultaneously: Ball A is thrown upward at 15 m/s from ground level, Ball B is dropped from 25 m height. When and where do they meet? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.markscheme_answer: Position A: y_A = 15t - 5t². Position B: y_B = 25 - 5t². When they meet: 15t - 5t² = 25 - 5t² → 15t = 25 → t = 5/3 s. Height: y = 15(5/3) - 5(25/9) = 25 - 125/9 = 100/9 ≈ 11.1 m

questions.question_text: A 2 kg object experiences a net force of 10 N. What is its acceleration?
A 5 kg box rests on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of static friction is 0.4. What is the maximum horizontal force that can be applied before the box moves? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.markscheme_answer: F_max = μN = μmg = 0.4 × 5 × 10 = 20 N

questions.question_text: A 3 kg object moving at 4 m/s collides with a stationary 1 kg object. They stick together. Find their common velocity after collision.
questions.markscheme_answer: Conservation of momentum: m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ = (m₁+m₂)v. 3×4 + 0 = 4v → v = 3 m/s

questions.question_text: A 2 kg block on a 30° incline is connected by a massless rope over a pulley to a hanging 3 kg mass. Find the acceleration of the system. (μ = 0.2, g = 10 m/s²)
questions.markscheme_answer: For hanging mass: 30 - T = 3a. For block: T - 2g(sin30° + μcos30°) = 2a. T - 10 - 0.2×2×10×0.866 = 2a. T - 13.46 = 2a. Solving: a = (30 - 13.46)/5 = 3.3 m/s²

questions.question_text: A rocket of initial mass 1000 kg ejects gas at 500 m/s relative to the rocket at a rate of 5 kg/s. What is the initial acceleration of the rocket if it launches vertically? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.markscheme_answer: Thrust = v_exhaust × dm/dt = 500 × 5 = 2500 N. Weight = 1000 × 10 = 10000 N. Net force = 2500 - 10000 = -7500 N (cannot lift off initially). If thrust exceeds weight: a = (F - mg)/m

questions.question_text: A 10 N force moves an object 5 m in the direction of the force. Calculate the work done.
A 2 kg ball is dropped from 20 m. What is its speed just before hitting the ground? (g = 10 m/s²)
A 1500 kg car accelerates from rest to 20 m/s in 10 s. Calculate the average power developed.
A spring with k = 200 N/m is compressed 0.3 m. A 0.5 kg ball is placed against it and released. The ball then slides up a frictionless ramp. What maximum height does it reach?
questions.markscheme_answer: Spring PE = ½kx² = ½×200×0.09 = 9 J. At max height: mgh = 9 → h = 9/(0.5×10) = 1.8 m

questions.question_text: A roller coaster car of mass 500 kg starts from rest at height 40 m. It loses 20% of its energy to friction by the time it reaches a loop of radius 10 m. Find the normal force on the car at the top of the loop.
What type of heat transfer occurs primarily through electromagnetic waves?
questions.markscheme_answer: Radiation

questions.question_text: How much heat is needed to raise the temperature of 2 kg of water by 10°C? (c = 4200 J/kg·K)
A 0.5 kg block of copper at 100°C is placed in 2 kg of water at 20°C. Find the final equilibrium temperature. (c_copper = 400 J/kg·K, c_water = 4200 J/kg·K)
A metal rod of length 1 m and cross-sectional area 0.01 m² connects two reservoirs at 100°C and 0°C. If k = 50 W/m·K, calculate the rate of heat transfer.
A black body sphere of radius 0.1 m and emissivity 0.9 is at 500 K in surroundings at 300 K. Calculate the net power radiated. (σ = 5.67×10⁻⁸ W/m²·K⁴)
What is the relationship between wave speed (v), frequency (f), and wavelength (λ)?
questions.markscheme_answer: v = fλ

questions.question_text: A wave has frequency 500 Hz and wavelength 0.68 m. Calculate the wave speed.
A transverse wave on a string has amplitude 5 cm and period 0.2 s. The string is 4 m long with 3 complete wavelengths. Find the wave speed.
Two coherent sources emit waves of wavelength 2 cm. A point P is 30 cm from one source and 34 cm from the other. Is there constructive or destructive interference at P?
questions.markscheme_answer: Path difference = 34 - 30 = 4 cm = 2λ. Since path difference = nλ (n = 2), there is constructive interference.

questions.question_text: Light of wavelength 600 nm passes through a double slit with separation 0.1 mm. The screen is 2 m away. Calculate the distance between the central maximum and the third bright fringe.
What are the points of zero displacement in a standing wave called?
questions.markscheme_answer: Nodes

questions.question_text: A string fixed at both ends has length 1.2 m. What is the wavelength of the third harmonic?
questions.markscheme_answer: For nth harmonic: L = nλ/2. For n=3: λ = 2L/3 = 2.4/3 = 0.8 m

questions.question_text: A pipe open at both ends has length 0.85 m. The speed of sound is 340 m/s. What is the fundamental frequency?
questions.markscheme_answer: For open pipe: f₁ = v/(2L) = 340/(2×0.85) = 200 Hz

questions.question_text: A pipe closed at one end resonates at 170 Hz in its fundamental mode. What is the frequency of the next resonant mode? (Speed of sound = 340 m/s)
questions.markscheme_answer: Closed pipe: only odd harmonics. Next mode is 3rd harmonic: f₃ = 3f₁ = 3 × 170 = 510 Hz

questions.question_text: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz produce beats. A string resonates with the beat frequency. If the string has mass per unit length 0.01 kg/m and length 0.4 m, what tension produces resonance in the fundamental mode?
State Ohm's Law.
questions.markscheme_answer: V = IR (Voltage equals current times resistance)

questions.question_text: A 12 V battery is connected to a 4 Ω resistor. Calculate the current flowing.
Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω, and 6 Ω are connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance.
A cell of emf 6 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is connected to an external resistance of 2.5 Ω. Find the terminal voltage and power dissipated in the external resistor.
questions.markscheme_answer: I = E/(R+r) = 6/3 = 2 A. Terminal voltage V = E - Ir = 6 - 1 = 5 V. Power = I²R = 4 × 2.5 = 10 W

questions.question_text: In a Wheatstone bridge, R₁ = 100 Ω, R₂ = 200 Ω, R₃ = 150 Ω. What value of R₄ balances the bridge? If the galvanometer has resistance 50 Ω and the bridge is supplied by 6 V, find the galvanometer current when R₄ = 250 Ω.
questions.markscheme_answer: For balance: R₁/R₂ = R₃/R₄ → 100/200 = 150/R₄ → R₄ = 300 Ω. When R₄ = 250 Ω, bridge is unbalanced. Use Thevenin equivalent or mesh analysis to find galvanometer current.

questions.question_text:
The position–time diagrams of two objects, X and Y, are shown in the same graph. Which of the following is correct about the motion of X and Y?

A) X and Y move with equal speed ✓
B) X and Y move with equal velocity
C) X and Y have equal displacement
D) X and Y move in the same direction
questions.markscheme_answer: A) X and Y move with equal speed. Speed is the rate of change of distance. The magnitude of speed is scalar, so the negative sign on X's velocity does not affect its magnitude. Both have equal speed but opposite velocities.

questions.question_text:
A car accelerates uniformly on a straight road with a positive velocity. Three statements are given:

I. The acceleration is constant.
II. The magnitude of the car's average speed is equal to that of its average velocity.
III. The magnitude of the distance travelled by the car is longer than its displacement.

Which statements are correct?

A) I and II ✓
B) II only
C) I and III
D) II and III
questions.markscheme_answer: A) I and II. Uniform acceleration means constant acceleration (I). On a straight road, distance equals displacement, so average speed equals average velocity (II). Statement III is incorrect.

questions.question_text:
A rock is thrown vertically upwards from a cliff edge with initial speed u. It hits the ground with speed 2u. What is the total flight time?

A) 3u/g ✓
B) 2u/g
C) u/g
D) 4u/g
questions.markscheme_answer: A) 3u/g. Time up: t₁ = u/g (v = u - gt, where v = 0). Time down: t₂ = 2u/g (v = gt, final speed = 2u). Total = u/g + 2u/g = 3u/g

questions.question_text:
A student walks 900 m to school and 1100 m back home via a different route. What is the total distance and displacement?

A) Distance: 2000 m, Displacement: 0 m ✓
B) Distance: 0 m, Displacement: 2000 m
C) Distance: 2000 m, Displacement: 2000 m
D) Distance: 0 m, Displacement: 0 m
questions.markscheme_answer: A) Distance: 2000 m, Displacement: 0 m. Total distance = 900 + 1100 = 2000 m. Displacement is zero since she returns to her starting point.

questions.question_text:
Which correctly lists scalar and vector quantities?

A) Scalar: Distance and speed, Vector: Displacement and velocity ✓
B) Scalar: Displacement and velocity, Vector: Distance and speed
C) Scalar: Distance and velocity, Vector: Displacement and speed
D) Scalar: Displacement and speed, Vector: Distance and velocity
questions.markscheme_answer: A) Scalar: Distance and speed (no direction), Vector: Displacement and velocity (have direction).

questions.question_text:
An acceleration–time graph shows positive constant acceleration in interval I, then decreasing but positive acceleration in interval II. During which interval(s) does velocity increase?

A) I and II ✓
B) I only
C) II only
D) None
questions.markscheme_answer: A) I and II. In both intervals acceleration is positive, so velocity increases. In I it increases uniformly, in II it increases non-uniformly.

questions.question_text:
Which graph represents an object that does not move in any direction?

A) A horizontal line on a position-time graph ✓
B) A diagonal line on a position-time graph
C) A horizontal line on a velocity-time graph
D) A diagonal line on an acceleration-time graph
questions.markscheme_answer: A) A horizontal line on a position-time graph. When position doesn't change with time, the object is stationary. Note: zero acceleration doesn't mean no movement - it could be constant velocity.

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown vertically downwards. Its change of height equals the magnitude of its ____________.
questions.markscheme_answer: displacement. Since the stone moves vertically, displacement equals change in height.

questions.question_text: When a car moves with constant acceleration, its velocity changes at a ____________ rate.
questions.markscheme_answer: constant (or uniform). Constant acceleration means velocity changes by the same amount each second.

questions.question_text: A skydiver's speed reaches a constant value called ____________ speed.
questions.markscheme_answer: terminal. When air resistance equals weight, net force is zero and speed remains constant.

questions.question_text: When a car has constant velocity, its acceleration is ____________.
questions.markscheme_answer: zero. No change in velocity means zero acceleration.

questions.question_text: A race car accelerates from rest to 55 m/s in 5.0 s. Calculate the acceleration.
A race car starts from rest with acceleration 8.0 m/s². What distance is covered after 4.0 s?
Speed increases from 10.5 km/h to 99.8 km/h in 2.41 s. Calculate acceleration in m/s².
A ball is thrown at 20 m/s at 60° to the ground. What is its velocity at maximum height? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.markscheme_answer: At max height, vy = 0. Only horizontal component remains: vx = 20 × cos(60°) = 10 m/s

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown at 23.1 m/s at 30° to the ground. At point P (15.0 m horizontal distance), find the angle between velocity and horizontal. (g = 9.8 m/s²)
Calculate the average speed (in m/s) of a cyclist who completes a 120 km race in 3 hours, 45 minutes, and 20 seconds.
questions.markscheme_answer:
Distance $d = 120,000 \text{ m}$.
Time $t = (3 \times 3600) + (45 \times 60) + 20 = 10800 + 2700 + 20 = 13520 \text{ s}$.
Average speed $v = \frac{120,000}{13520} \approx 8.88 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

questions.question_text: A spaceship travels a distance of 450,000 km from Earth to the Moon in 72 hours, 10 minutes. What is its average speed in m/s?
questions.markscheme_answer:
Distance $d = 4.5 \times 10^8 \text{ m}$.
Time $t = (72 \times 3600) + (10 \times 60) = 259800 \text{ s}$.
Average speed $v = \frac{4.5 \times 10^8}{259800} \approx 1732 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

questions.question_text: A rock dropped from a bridge takes 1.45 s to hit the water below. Calculate the height of the bridge in meters. (Assume g = 9.81 m/s² and ignore air resistance)
questions.markscheme_answer:
Initial velocity $u = 0$.
Time $t = 1.45 \text{ s}$. Acceleration $a = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Height $s = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(9.81)(1.45)^2 \approx 10.3 \text{ m}$.

questions.question_text: A small ball is dropped from a cliff of height 45.0 m. How long does it take to reach the ground in seconds? (Use g = 9.81 m/s²)
questions.markscheme_answer:
Displacement $s = 45.0 \text{ m}$. Initial velocity $u = 0$.
Acceleration $a = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
$s = \frac{1}{2}at^2 \implies 45.0 = \frac{1}{2}(9.81)t^2$.
$t = \sqrt{\frac{90.0}{9.81}} \approx 3.03 \text{ s}$.

questions.question_text: A drone drops a package from a height of 120 m. What is the package's instantaneous velocity magnitude just before it hits the ground? (Use g = 9.81 m/s²)
questions.markscheme_answer:
Initial velocity $u = 0$.
Acceleration $a = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Displacement $s = 120 \text{ m}$.
$v^2 = 0^2 + 2(9.81)(120) = 2354.4$.
Therefore, $v = \sqrt{2354.4} \approx 48.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

questions.question_text: A cart rolling down an inclined plane passes point A with a velocity of 2.5 m/s. A short time later, it passes point B with a velocity of 6.1 m/s. If the distance between A and B is 8.0 m, calculate the acceleration of the cart.
questions.markscheme_answer:
Initial velocity $u = 2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Final velocity $v = 6.1 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Distance $s = 8.0 \text{ m}$.
Using $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$, we have $6.1^2 = 2.5^2 + 2(a)(8.0)$.
$37.21 = 6.25 + 16a \implies 30.96 = 16a \implies a \approx 1.935 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.

questions.question_text: A ball rolling down a slope passes a point P with a velocity of 1.2 m/s. It passes point Q with a velocity of 2.6 m/s. If it took 1.4 s to go from P to Q, determine the distance PQ.
questions.markscheme_answer:
With constant acceleration, average velocity $v_{avg} = \frac{u+v}{2} = \frac{1.2 + 2.6}{2} = 1.9 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
The distance is $s = v_{avg} \times t = 1.9 \times 1.4 = 2.66 \text{ m}$.

questions.question_text: An aircraft accelerates from rest along a runway and takes off with a velocity of 75.0 m/s. Its acceleration during this time is 3.20 m/s². Calculate the distance along the runway that the aircraft needs to travel before take-off.
questions.markscheme_answer:
Initial velocity $u = 0$.
Final velocity $v = 75.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Acceleration $a = 3.20 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
$75.0^2 = 0 + 2(3.20)s \implies 5625 = 6.4s \implies s \approx 878.9 \text{ m}$.

questions.question_text: An ocean-going cruiser can decelerate no quicker than 0.0032 m/s². Determine the minimum distance (in meters) needed to stop if the ship is travelling at 5.14 m/s (10 knots).
questions.markscheme_answer:
Initial velocity $u = 5.14 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Final velocity $v = 0$.
Acceleration $a = -0.0032 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
$0 = 5.14^2 + 2(-0.0032)s \implies 26.4196 = 0.0064s \implies s \approx 4128 \text{ m}$.

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of 6.2 m/s from a balcony 8.5 m above the ground. With what speed would it hit the ground? (Use g = 9.81 m/s²)
questions.markscheme_answer:
Let upwards be positive.
$u = +6.2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. $a = -9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
The final displacement is $s = -8.5 \text{ m}$ (since it hits the ground below the starting point).
$v^2 = 6.2^2 + 2(-9.81)(-8.5) = 38.44 + 166.77 = 205.21$.
$v = \sqrt{205.21} \approx 14.3 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. Note the speed is the magnitude.

questions.question_text: A small rock is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of 22 m/s. Calculate the *later* time (in seconds) when its velocity magnitude is exactly 10 m/s. (Use g = 9.81 m/s²)
questions.markscheme_answer:
The *later* time means it is coming back down.
On the way down, the velocity is $v = -10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Using $v = u + at$, we have $-10 = 22 - 9.81t \implies 9.81t = 32 \implies t \approx 3.26 \text{ s}$.

questions.question_text: The velocity-time graph below represents a car's journey. What is the total distance traveled in 13 seconds?
questions.markscheme_answer:
Distance = area of triangle = $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$
Distance = $\frac{1}{2} \times 13 \times 18 = 117.0$ m.

questions.question_text: The velocity-time graph below shows the motion of an object over 17 seconds. Determine the object's acceleration during the first 6 seconds.

a = $\frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{15 - 0}{6 - 0} = 2.5$ m/s².

a = $\frac{0 - 24}{10 - 7} = -8.0$ m/s².
Magnitude = 8.0 m/s².
